piece_read.reader: salon owners deciding whether to ask for a deposit at booking
points: Bookings that asked for a 20% deposit had a 3% no-show rate, against 11% for bookings without one.
Asking for a deposit cut completed online bookings by only 4%.
Clients accepted the deposit more often when the policy was shown before they picked a time, not at checkout.
All three featured salons refund the deposit when a client cancels at least 24 hours ahead.

findings: LinkedIn Page earns the most per post: 98.6 engaged-visit equivalents per piece (38.4 engaged sessions and 2.36 key events), so it leads on day 0.

Facebook Page reaches nearly as many posts as LinkedIn (10 against 11) but turns few visits into sign-ups (0.5 key events per piece against 2.36 on LinkedIn): it keeps its 2 slots because it is proven, and it ranks 3.

The salon owners forum is thin evidence (2 posts reached) with the most key events per piece of any channel (2.5 per piece): one slot on day 2, and the day 7 rule adds a second if it beats 30 engaged sessions.

Meta Ads buys an engaged visit for $7.82 against $17.92 on LinkedIn Ads, so the boost goes on Meta if the day 3 gate passes. Closing the 54-visit gap would take $423; the $400 cap buys about 51, so the plan expects 217 of the 220 goal and says so.
unknowns: Reddit and the forum can't be booked through the scheduler; they are posted by hand.
Medium has no past data, so it gets one test and no expected number.
